title: The five realms as a path
word: The five realms as a path
hookLine: duty, knowledge, effort, grace, truth: a map of growth

cards: A trail map at the foot of a mountain has a red dot on it: you are here. Without the dot, the map is just a pretty drawing. With it, you can see how far you've come and what's next.

Yesterday jumped straight to the top of a mountain in Japji. Today goes back to the trailhead and walks the whole thing. Sikh readers have read Guru Nanak's realms as stages of growth, a map of the inner climb.
And the map asks: where's your dot?

teach.b: Duty comes first: Dharam Khand. Japji says, in paraphrase, that amid nights and seasons and days, wind, water and fire, the earth was set as a home for dharma, right living.
Here deeds are weighed, each judged by what it does. It's the ground floor.

Then knowledge: Gian Khand, where, Japji says, knowledge blazes, opening on a universe without edges, worlds and suns and beings beyond count. Readers take that vastness as cutting the ego down to size.
Then effort: Saram Khand, whose language, Japji says, is beauty; there the mind and understanding are shaped and refined. Readers differ on saram: some hear effort, some beauty, some humility.
All three describe a self being worked on, like a craftsman's piece on the bench.

teach.h: KARAM AND SACH: GRACE, THEN TRUTH.
teach.b: Then Karam Khand, whose language is power: here live warriors filled with the One's strength. Here karam is read as grace, the other reading of the word we met with the robe and the door.
And last, Sach Khand, home of the Formless. Duty, knowledge, effort, grace, truth. Readers notice a turn at the fourth step: in their reading, the climber stops climbing and is carried.
Effort gets you up the slope, they say, and grace takes you over the ridge. Some Sikh readers stress that the realms aren't a ladder you finish, but rooms you may move between on any day.
Either way, the map is for one honest question.

how: Sikhs recite Japji Sahib each morning, and its closing pauris describe the realms of duty, knowledge, effort, grace and truth, which Sikh teachers explain as stages of spiritual growth.

games.q: what does “the five realms as a path” mean?
o: five rules a new Sikh promises to keep
five stages of the inner climb, from duty to truth
five holy cities every Sikh hopes to visit once

games.q: the five realms: tap the pairs.
p: duty: the earth as a home for dharma

s: the word saram has only one accepted meaning
some hear effort, some beauty, some humility.
in the map, grace comes after effort
duty, knowledge, effort, then grace, then truth.
Japji describes Gian Khand as a small, tidy world
knowledge blazes there, opening on worlds beyond any count.

games.q: you've walked Japji's realms of duty, knowledge and effort. what is the fourth realm named for?
games.why: Karam Khand is read as the realm of grace: in that reading, effort gets you up the slope, and grace takes you over the ridge.

practice: Walk the realms slowly in your mind, asking without grading yourself: am I doing what's right in front of me, do I remember how big the world is, am I letting myself be shaped, am I leaving room to be carried?
Notice which room feels like where you stand today, and breathe there for a while.

wordCard.voice: The five realms as a path. Dharam, gian, saram, karam and sach: duty, knowledge, effort, grace and truth, read by Sikh teachers as a map of the inner climb. Today's word.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: khand, realm or region; Japji names Dharam, Gian, Saram, Karam and Sach Khand.

carryVoice: Your line: where am I. A map helps most once the dot is on it. Back tomorrow, same hill.
